finding.claim: OS command injection in /ping: the unauthenticated `host` query parameter is concatenated into a shell command string passed to child_process.exec, which runs via /bin/sh. An attacker can append shell metacharacters (e.g. `;`, `&&`, `$(...)`, backticks) to run arbitrary commands as the server user. Output is returned in the response, so it is not blind. Passing an array `host` (?host=a&host=b) is also stringified by concatenation.

trace.note: Route handler for GET /ping, no auth middleware
req.query.host concatenated directly into the command string and passed to exec(), which spawns a shell
stdout is returned to the client via res.send(out), so command output is exfiltrated; e.g. /ping?host=127.0.0.1;id returns the output of id

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, allowlist, or escaping on host. No authentication or authorization middleware on the app. No rate limiting. exec is used rather than execFile with an argv array. Also checked /version (execFile with a fixed argv, no user input) and /uptime (exec with a constant string); neither is exploitable.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec() (shell) with no validation, auth, or middleware in the file, and tools.js:11 returns stdout. For `;id` the shell exit status is that of the last command, so the err branch at line 8 is not hit and the output is returned.

verdict_facts.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec() (shell) with no auth, validation or escaping anywhere in tools.js (the only file), and tools.js:11 returns stdout, so `;id` gives output when the final command exits 0.
